response:
REFLECTION ON GEN-0 EVIDENCE
All four evaluated signals produced FMB t-stats in the hypothesized direction but FF5 long-short alphas with the *opposite* sign (e.g. CashYield_Per_Capital_Intensity: fmb +2.75, alpha −3.2%/yr with t = −2.9; Expensive_Capacity_Expander: fmb −3.77, alpha +2.1%). The diagnosis is factor spanning, not noise: a "cheap + conservative-investment" sort loads heavily positive on both HML and CMA (and often RMW), so FF5 explains more than the raw spread and the residual tips negative. Two responses follow: (i) build the interaction from measures that are *not* the FF5 factor axes (enterprise-value yield rather than B/M; M&A/goodwill, inventory-vs-sales, or investment volatility rather than asset growth), and (ii) express both legs *relative to the firm's own history* so the portfolio is not permanently parked in cheap, low-growth stocks. I also include one deliberate orientation flip, since the repeated alpha sign reversal is itself evidence that, after HML/CMA, cheap firms that keep reinvesting may beat cheap firms starving their capital base.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: EVYield_x_Inorganic_Restraint
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(aqc, 0), DELTA(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), 1)), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms cheap on a whole-capital basis (high EBITDA-to-enterprise-value) that also refuse to buy growth through acquisitions and goodwill accumulation are disciplined allocators, whereas richly valued serial acquirers capitalize deal narratives that later impair.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: EBITDA/EV prices debt and cash as well as equity, so it is materially less collinear with HML than book-to-market, and acquisition/goodwill expansion is a channel that CMA's asset-growth definition captures only weakly — together this attacks the gen-0 factor-spanning problem at its source. Zero-acquisition firms tie in the discipline rank, but the continuous EV-yield rank still orders the product within those ties, so the long leg remains well populated.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: OwnHistory_Cheap_x_OwnHistory_Restraint
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Mispricing arises when a firm is cheap relative to its *own* recent valuation history at the same time as its reinvestment rate sits near its own five-year low: this is the signature of a business the market has re-rated downward while management has quietly stopped feeding low-return projects, and the correction is slow.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Both legs are firm-relative, so the sorted portfolio rotates across the cross-section instead of permanently holding statically cheap, low-growth names, which should sharply reduce the HML and CMA loadings that absorbed the gen-0 spreads and leave any mispricing in the FF5 alpha. It directly tests whether the gen-0 alpha sign problem was a framing (cross-sectional vs own-history) issue rather than a mechanism failure.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Quadrant_Cheap_Disciplined_Vs_Expensive_Builder
EXPRESSION: SUB(MUL(INDICATOR(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.5), INDICATOR(NEG(IND_ZSCORE(GROWTH(ppegt, 1))), 0)), MUL(INDICATOR(NEG(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), 0.5), INDICATOR(IND_ZSCORE(GROWTH(ppegt, 1)), 0)))
HYPOTHESIS: The mispricing is concentrated in two corners of the valuation-investment plane: decisively cheap firms with below-industry capacity growth (+1) and decisively expensive firms with above-industry capacity growth (−1); everything in between carries no information and should be held flat.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: A three-valued corner signal builds the long and short legs only from firms exhibiting both conditions, which maximizes the interaction content per position instead of diluting it with the linear main effects that FF5 already prices. Its outcome is diagnostic: if this concentrated version also delivers a negative FF5 alpha, the story's orientation, not the construction, is what fails.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Value_Corroborated_By_Reinvestment
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent)))
HYPOTHESIS: Among cheap firms, managers who continue to reinvest at a healthy rate in existing plant are signaling that returns on capital still exceed the cost of capital, while cheap firms letting the capital base decay are genuine value traps in secular decline; symmetrically, the worst combination is a rich multiple with no reinvestment to justify it.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is a deliberate orientation flip motivated by evidence, not taste: every gen-0 "cheap-and-restrained" construction earned a negative FF5 alpha, implying that once HML and CMA premia are removed the residual favors cheap reinvestors. Using capx/ppent (a reinvestment-intensity ratio, not asset growth) keeps the investment leg off the CMA axis so the test is informative about the residual rather than the factor.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Value_x_Inventory_Sales_Mismatch
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(NEG(SUB(GROWTH(invt, 1), GROWTH(sale, 1)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Working-capital investment reveals demand misjudgment: cheap firms whose inventories are growing faster than sales are accumulating unsold product and will disappoint, while cheap firms whose inventory grows slower than sales are converting discipline into genuine operating leverage.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Inventory growth net of sales growth is an investment-discipline measure orthogonal to both total asset growth (CMA) and capital expenditure, so the resulting spread should carry little mechanical factor loading and any premium must show up as alpha. It also tests a real-operations channel of "discipline" distinct from every fixed-capital construction in the archive.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: CashYield_x_Investment_Stability
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(capx, at), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Discipline is a second-moment property: cheap firms whose capital-spending intensity is steady year after year follow a coherent plan, whereas cheap firms with erratic, stop-start capital budgets are reacting to shocks and financing constraints, and their cash-flow yield is not dependable.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Investment volatility is uncorrelated by construction with the level of investment, so this spread should be close to CMA-neutral while still expressing a valuation-times-investment interaction, addressing the spanning problem from a different angle than Signals 1 and 2. The five-year window costs coverage, so its result should be read alongside Signal 2 to judge whether long-window constructions are viable in this sample.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---CRITIQUE EVYield_x_Inorganic_Restraint---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Genuinely distinct from the archive — the enterprise-multiple valuation leg and the acquisition/goodwill-accumulation discipline leg are both economically coherent and only weakly spanned by HML/CMA — though the EV denominator can go near-zero or negative for net-cash firms and should be winsorized or floored before ranking, and the aqc/gdwl COALESCE-to-zero mass will leave a large tied block in the discipline rank.

---CRITIQUE OwnHistory_Cheap_x_OwnHistory_Restraint---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The framing (own-history rather than cross-sectional) is a legitimately different construction, but TS_RANK of book-to-market over five years is driven almost entirely by the price denominator and is therefore a near-mechanical proxy for the well-documented five-year long-term reversal anomaly, and a 5-point time-series rank is too coarse to sort a cross-section cleanly.

---CRITIQUE Quadrant_Cheap_Disciplined_Vs_Expensive_Builder---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a discretized re-expression of the already-tested Value_x_Capex_Deceleration / Expensive_Capacity_Expander mechanism rather than a new one — the proposal's own reasoning concedes it is a diagnostic re-run of the same story — and collapsing to {-1,0,+1} discards information while making leg membership and portfolio composition highly unstable at the z-score cutoffs.

---CRITIQUE Value_Corroborated_By_Reinvestment---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The positive expected sign on high capx/ppent among cheap firms contradicts the well-established capital-investment anomaly (Titman-Wei-Xie), and the stated motivation — that gen-0 alphas came out negative so the orientation should be flipped — is a post-hoc sign fit on the same data rather than an economic mechanism, applied to a trivially simple product of two standard ranks.

---CRITIQUE Value_x_Inventory_Sales_Mismatch---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The interaction is new to this archive and the working-capital channel is meaningfully distinct from the fixed-capital constructions already tested, but the discipline leg is essentially the Lev-Thiagarajan / Thomas-Zhang inventory-versus-sales fundamental signal, so the burden is on the interaction (not the leg) to add anything, and GROWTH ratios on small or zero inventory bases will need trimming.

---CRITIQUE CashYield_x_Investment_Stability---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A second-moment discipline leg is a genuinely different angle from the archive's level- and change-based capex constructions, but the claim that capex volatility is "uncorrelated by construction" with capex level is simply false (dispersion scales with level, so the leg will partially reproduce a low-investment tilt), and the five-year window plus the earlier EBITDA-yield result suggest coverage and sign risk should be checked before reading much into it.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Value_x_Capex_Drawdown_From_Own_Peak
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(capx, at), 5), RATIO(capx, at)), ADD(0.02, TS_MAX(RATIO(capx, at), 5)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Deliberate retrenchment is best measured as how far current capital-spending intensity sits below the firm's own five-year peak: cheap firms operating well below their historical investment peak have voluntarily exited the expansion phase of their capital cycle, and the market is slow to re-rate the resulting free cash flow.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: The own-history framing is now applied only to the investment leg, where it is driven by real capital-spending decisions, while valuation is measured cross-sectionally with sales-to-price — this removes the previous version's mechanical dependence on a five-year price path and hence its overlap with long-term reversal. The drawdown is a continuous fraction in roughly [0,1] rather than a five-point time-series rank, so it sorts the cross-section finely, and the 0.02 floor keeps firms with negligible peak capex from producing unstable values.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Value_x_Capital_Productivity_Gain
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(sale, ppegt), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Discipline shows up as squeezing more revenue out of installed capital rather than as the level of spending: cheap firms whose sales per dollar of gross plant is rising are extracting returns from assets already in place, whereas expensive firms whose capital productivity is deteriorating are adding capacity the market has already paid for but demand has not filled.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This abandons the capex-level/asset-growth mechanism entirely and substitutes the productivity of installed capital, a channel none of the archived signals touches and one that is close to orthogonal to CMA, so any premium should survive FF5 rather than be absorbed by it. It is continuous and finely ranked, avoiding the unstable {-1,0,+1} leg membership of the quadrant construction it replaces.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: EarnYield_x_Unproductive_Expansion_Penalty
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(NEG(MUL(RATIO(DELTA(ppent, 1), LAG(ppegt, 1)), INDICATOR(NEG(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(sale, ppegt))), 0)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Not all investment is undisciplined: expansion is value-destroying mainly when undertaken by firms whose installed capital is already below-average productive. Cheap firms that either shrink or expand only where capital productivity is high are disciplined allocators; cheap firms expanding a low-productivity asset base are the true empire-builders.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: The orientation is restored to the theoretically and empirically supported direction (penalizing investment, consistent with Titman-Wei-Xie), so no post-hoc sign fitting is involved. The investment leg is a constructed measure — *net* capacity expansion relative to installed gross plant, which strips maintenance/depreciation capex — gated by an industry-relative productivity indicator, so the penalty applies only where over-investment is economically plausible rather than to every high-capex firm.
